So my wife and I had a lot of uncomfortable, middle-of-the-night conversations about what to do. In addition to the two books I mentioned in the original post, I also ended up reading The Happy Sleeper by Heather Turgeon and Julie Wright
Four months later: a third book.
In the end, we built a version of the Ferber Method combined with many of the methods from The Happy Sleeper.

After the nighttime routine is done, we set a timer for 10 min. If she is crying/extra fussy at the end of the time, one of us goes in for a "check-up" (normally it's me who does the first one), where we pick her up, sing her the same lullabies again
The first week was what you might expect, though she adapted surprisingly quickly. Now, unless something is going on with her, she falls asleep within the first 10-20 min and only needs one check-in.
